turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `composition` (absorber), `architecture` (n-i-p =
regular, p-i-n = inverted), `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode),
`etl` (electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Each row is a device
CONFIGURATION whose efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently
fabricated cells, so it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single
champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_open_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_open_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
High-efficiency cells in the training set cluster around FA-rich mixed-cation lead iodides/bromides (FAMAPbBrI, CsFAMAPbBrI, CsFAPbI, FAMAPbI). These absorbers sit near the Shockley–Queisser optimum, form the black photoactive phase, and avoid the deep traps that accompany Sn oxidation or Bi/Sb vacancy disorder. Everything else (pure Br, Sn, Bi, 2-D-only, carbon mesoscopic) is therefore discarded.

Selective contacts that repeatedly appear above ~19 % are:
- n-side: SnO2 (planar or QD) or compact+mesoporous TiO2, often finished with a C60-based SAM or thin fullerene (cascade alignment, trap passivation, hole blocking);
- p-side: doped Spiro-MeOTAD (n-i-p) or PTAA (p-i-n), never PEDOT:PSS (acidic, poor WF);
- electrode: Au (n-i-p) or Cu (p-i-n); Ag only when a BCP or MoO3 diffusion barrier is present.

Interface recombination is the remaining loss channel. The highest training values (22.9 %, 22.0 %, 19.7 %) all add a low-dimensional capping layer or a molecular SAM that terminates under-coordinated Pb and A-site vacancies.

Applying those constraints to the pool:

- **c015** (CsFAMAPbBrI|(EPA)PbI / mp-TiO2 / Spiro / Au) is a 3-D/2-D bilayer on the same scaffold that produced the 22.9 % champion. The EPA-based 2-D sheet passivates the HTL interface while the bulk triple-cation film supplies high mobility and the correct band gap.
- **c085** (CsFAMAPbBrI / PTAA|PFN-Br / C60|BCP / Cu) is the inverted analogue of the 20.1–20.3 % cells, with an extra conjugated-polyelectrolyte dipole that improves wetting and further lowers interface recombination; Cu is chemically more inert toward iodide than Ag.
- **c093** (CsFAMAPbBrI / PTAA / PCBM|BCP / Ag) is essentially the 20.3 % training stack; BCP still protects the Ag electrode.
- **c061** (CsFAPbI / SnO2-c|C60-SAM / Spiro / Au) combines the 1.5 eV, MA-free absorber that already reached 20.2 % with a covalently bound C60-SAM that passivates SnO2 oxygen vacancies and provides cascade electron extraction.
- **c008** (FAMAPbI / SnO2-c / Spiro / Au, sequential spin-coating) is the classic planar n-i-p recipe; the double deposition step yields compact, large-grain FA-rich films and the Au/Spiro contact is ohmic.

All five therefore combine an optimal absorber, band-aligned selective contacts, a chemically inert electrode, and an explicit recombination-suppressing interface.

Final: c015, c085, c093, c061, c008
